# Tumor Evolution and Adaptive Therapy

## Big picture (analogy)

Sensitive and resistant cells **compete** under treatment pressure—like flowers and weeds under weeding.

- Continuous high pressure can eliminate sensitive cells and leave resistant ones dominant.
- **Adaptive therapy** deliberately eases pressure at times so sensitive cells can again outcompete resistant ones (“breathing room”).

**ITH (intratumor heterogeneity):** not all cells in a tumor are identical.

## Branched expansion

:::{.columns}

:::{.column width="70%"}
@nowell1976clonal proposed tumor evolution model. Tumors expand via:

 - Expansion in branches
 - Multiple subclones with splitting mechanisms
  
:::

## Implication of ITH - diagnostics

**How we monitor (one sentence each)**

- **Radiomics / habitat imaging:** extract spatial patterns from scans that may reflect different tumor “neighborhoods”
- **ctDNA (circulating tumor DNA):** measure tumor-derived DNA fragments in blood over time

:::{.columns}

:::{.column width=48%}
- Spatial and temporal monitoring of tumor cells
  - Radiomics, habitat imaging @sala2017unravelling
- Longitudinal tracking of cancer development 
  - Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) @kim2022dynamic

## Implication of ITH - Lamarckism
:::{.columns}

:::{.column width="48%"}
- Treatment-resistance is not simply Darwinian evolution. [@valcz2025adaptive]
- Evidence: Adaptation to low-dose treatment in a short time
- Epigenetic plasticity:  Modifying epigenetic features, transfer, and inherit among tumor cell 
:::

:::{.column width="48%"}
![Green: treatment sensitive cell @pisco2013non](/assets/images/adt/lamarkian-dye.png){width=60%}
:::

:::

![Lamarckism from @bell2020principles](/assets/images/adt/lamarkian.png){width=60%}

## Evolutionary therapeutics

:::{.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

**Adaptive therapy**

Giving "breathing room" to drug-sensitive tumors. During the low-dosage periods, drug-sensitive cells can outcompete resistant ones.

- Adjust time (Intermittent therapy)
- Dosage 

**Applications**

- Breast cancer [@enriquez2016exploiting] 
- Prostate cancer [@zhang2017integrating]

:::

:::{.column width="48%"}

![Adaptive therapy, figure from @mcgehee2024mathematical](/assets/images/adt/adaptive.png)

:::

:::

## Monitoring tumor progress

- Adaptive therapy relies on close monitoring of tumor progression
- Current practice:
  - Monitoring on tumor biomarkers
  - Monitoring on dosage levels of the drug in the blood

|  Tumor type | Monitor parameter | Study |
|  ---------- | ----------------- | ----- |
| Ovarian cancer | Serum biomarker + Tumor size  | @mukherjee2024study |
| Prostate cancer | Blood biomarker  | @zhang2017integrating |
| Melanoma | Tumor size | @smalley2019leveraging |
| Breast cancer | Tumor size | @enriquez2016exploiting |

- Implication: Some tumors are not good targets for adaptive therapy due to the management cost

## Adaptive strategy

Designing strategy to turn on- and off- the therapy also varies


| Study | Type | Rule |
| ------- | ----- | --------- |
| @mukherjee2024study | Continuous | Proportion to biomarkers |
| @zhang2017integrating | Intermittent | Proportion to tumor size |
| @smalley2019leveraging | Intermittent | Tumor size + mathematical simulation |
| @enriquez2016exploiting | Continuous | Proportion to tumor size |

## Benefits of adaptive therapy

:::{.columns}

:::{.column width="48%"}

- Delayed drug resistance
  - Delayed tumor progression
- Better clinical outcome 
- Improve quality of life @hussain2013intermittent
  - Side effects of the treatment may be reduced during off-cycles

:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
![Better outcome in metastatic colorectal cancer @avallone2025intermittent](/assets/images/adt/intermittent%20threrapy.png)
:::

:::

## Challenges in adaptive therapy

- Identifying heterogeneity in the tumor and monitoring the response to the treatment
- Ultimately kill all cancer cells is extremely challenging 
  - **Analogy**: Antibiotics, antiviral drug resistance
- Adaptive therapy tries to
  - Make the tumor manageable
  - **Not** necessarily fully cure cancer
